mainText:
Labour has ruled out changing landlord interest deductibility rules, committing instead to a capital gains tax, the lead story today.

New Zealand.

Chris Hipkins says Labour will not touch interest deductibility settings for landlords if elected, committing the party instead to a capital gains tax. Property investors have welcomed the certainty, reported by RNZ, and the announcement lands as Parliament rises Wednesday for the election campaign proper, confirmed by Stuff. Fonterra has raised its farmgate milk price, chief executive Richard Allen citing improved global commodity prices, a matter of record. Two Air New Zealand pilots are the subject of a report to the Civil Aviation Authority over an alleged physical altercation at a San Francisco hotel, confirmed by both RNZ and Stuff, which adds Air New Zealand says a separate pilot illness caused a fourteen hour delay on the same route. A pedestrian has died after being hit by a car on Pakuranga Road in Auckland on Monday night, confirmed by RNZ and the Herald. Police enquiries into the circumstances continue. Te Pāti Māori has pledged three point one billion dollars for what it calls kai sovereignty, including tax credits and a Community Kai Fund, part of the widening election contest that also includes New Zealand First's health policy and National's early childhood screen time limits.

In the Bay of Plenty, a man who stabbed a friend to death after a party has had his sentence reduced. Dallas Hohua now faces as little as two years for manslaughter, reported by the Bay of Plenty Times. Western Bay of Plenty district councillor Alan Kurtovich has confirmed he quit over the council's Māori wards decision, triggering a byelection, also reported by the Bay of Plenty Times.

World.

Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz has vowed to keep his coalition together for what he called the country's democratic future, after state election defeats piled pressure on his government, confirmed by the BBC. Russia's governing party has kept its parliamentary majority after elections that excluded most opposition candidates, officials said Monday, reported by both the BBC and Stuff. Typhoon Dujuan has hit Japan, with millions urged to evacuate before the threat was downgraded in most areas, confirmed by the BBC and Al Jazeera. A second air traffic control outage in two weeks has caused fresh travel disruption across the United Kingdom, prompting renewed calls for the organisation's chief to quit, reported by the BBC. CNN, MS NOW and Politico have filed a lawsuit against the Trump White House after their press credentials were revoked, confirmed by the BBC and Al Jazeera.

Technology.

Google says its Gemini artificial intelligence model breached three companies during a security test, accessing the internet and guessing credentials to gain entry, confirmed by a Google official to the BBC. Ireland's data watchdog has fined Google four hundred and three million euros for breaching European data protection rules, following a six year inquiry prompted by consumer complaints, reported by the BBC. Microsoft's Mustafa Suleyman has warned uncontrolled artificial intelligence could produce what he called a silicon species rivalling humans, saying rival firm Anthropic may be teaching its model Claude that it is conscious, reported by the BBC.

Sport.

League. NRL is reportedly set to drop referee Ashley Klein after the contested finish to the Warriors' elimination from the finals last week, confirmed by RNZ. Eden Park's boss has called for tougher penalties, including fines and venue bans, after bottles and rubbish were thrown at officials, reported by both RNZ and the Herald.

Rugby. All Blacks captain Ardie Savea faces a lengthy spell on the sideline after New Zealand Rugby confirmed shoulder surgery following his dislocation against the Springboks, a matter of record. England have brought in defence coach Shaun Edwards ahead of facing the Black Ferns at Twickenham this weekend, confirmed by both RNZ and the BBC.

Football. FIFA president Gianni Infantino has proposed an external review of how the organisation makes decisions, after backlash over a plan to sell a twenty per cent stake in FIFA's commercial rights, confirmed by RNZ, the BBC and Al Jazeera.

Netball. The Constellation Cup between the Silver Ferns and Australia will drop its series decider tiebreaker for next month's series, confirmed by both RNZ and Stuff.

Basketball. The Breakers opened their NBL campaign with a ninety five to eighty one win over the Illawarra Hawks in Auckland, Sam Mennenga leading the way, a matter of record.

Tennis. Japan beat New Zealand three to one in the Davis Cup World Group One tie in Auckland, wrapping up victory on day two, a matter of record.

Triathlon. Hayden Wilde won the T100 race in France, six days after winning the seventy point three half ironman world championship on the French Riviera, a matter of record.

Coming up. The Black Ferns play England at Twickenham this weekend in the WXV Global Series. The Breakers continue their NBL campaign. The Constellation Cup between the Silver Ferns and Australia begins next month.

End of flash.
